notes: Direct was easy everywhere (always the shortest, statement-only reply), companion usually opened by naming something the person got right or added a playful line, and the Logos challenger was signposted by 'the part to distrust' or 'what result would change your mind'. The hard split was Core thinker vs challenger: no Core reply asks a question and both lead with the weak point and steelman, so I separated them on relentless rebuttal and evidence/test framing (challenger) versus Socratic reframes and dry humour (thinker); c5 has no warmth cues at all, and in c6/l6 the quieted styles nearly converge.
